clue.text: Hopelessness entering Dr Matt Fink's second letters on psychic power

indicators.note: going into something means these letters end up placed inside another word
only the letter in second place of each named word is taken

blocks.note: taken as written, the abbreviation for doctor
second letters of Matt and Fink

explanation.surface: Matt Fink (Dr Fink), keyboardist with Prince's Revolution, seems to be sinking into despair.
explanation.walkthrough: The psychic power goes first and the two second letters sit 'on' it, after it; that whole run then enters DR to make DESPAIR.
explanation.definitionFit: Despair is a total loss of hope, so the noun is a straight synonym of hopelessness.

clue.text: Imagined setter being enveloped by fear

indicators.note: something enveloped is wrapped inside something else, so one word sits within another

blocks.note: the crossword setter refers to themself as me

explanation.surface: Someone pictured a terrifying puzzle-maker, overcome with fear.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter of a crossword conventionally calls themself me.
explanation.definitionFit: To have dreamed something is to have imagined it, as a past-tense synonym.

clue.text: The beautiful ones meld with poseurs, mingling

indicators.note: things mingling are mixed together, so these letters get jumbled up

explanation.surface: Beautiful people mix and mingle with pretentious types at a party; 'The Beautiful Ones' is also a Prince song.
explanation.definitionFit: Supermodels are famous fashion models chosen for their looks, so they are a fair example of beautiful people.

clue.text: Of Prince, The Revolution say "a fellow with radical style"

indicators.note: radical means drastically changed, so the letters of the next word are rearranged

blocks.note: the prefix co- means fellow, as in co-worker

explanation.surface: A fan describes a member of Prince's band The Revolution as a fellow with a radical style.
explanation.walkthrough: The Revolution was Prince's backing band in the 1980s; the definition is a whole phrase, with 'say' marking them as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Acolytes are devoted followers or assistants, and a backing band could be described as a star's attendants.

clue.text: See 6
Delay describing quiet victory for flapper

indicators.note: to describe a circle is to draw round it, so one word goes around the others

blocks.note: p for piano, quiet in music

explanation.surface: A hold-up in announcing a narrow win for a 1920s flapper girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flapper' suggests a 1920s young woman, but here it is anything that flaps its wings. A lapwing is a plover-like bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A lapwing is a bird, and birds flap their wings, so flapper is a cryptic description of the bird.

clue.text: They're reducing the light shed by city politicians on underworld figure

blocks.note: the Greek god of the underworld

explanation.surface: Politicians from a city cast a little light on a gangster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Underworld figure' suggests a gangster, but here it is the god who rules the Greek underworld.
explanation.definitionFit: Shades fitted over lamps soften and dim the glow a bulb gives off, which is what the description says.

clue.text: Regularly tape superb LPs: Blue every Cardigans album

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so letters are picked at a fixed spacing along the run

blocks.clueFragment: tape superb LPs: Blue every Cardigans
blocks.note: every third letter, starting with the third

explanation.surface: A music fan recording favourite records, from blues LPs to every album by the Swedish band The Cardigans.
explanation.walkthrough: The spacing here is every third letter, starting from the p in 'tape'. Purple Rain is Prince's 1984 album, the theme of this puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: Purple Rain is the famous 1984 record by Prince and The Revolution, so it is an example of an album.

clue.text: Roman historian not using Latin name of plant

indicators.note: not using a thing means leaving it out, so a letter is dropped

explanation.surface: A Roman writer of history who avoided Latin names for plants.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivy is a climbing evergreen plant, so the answer is an example of a plant.

clue.text: Gateshead lanes lead to kitchens in the marina

blocks.note: read as Gate's head: the first letter of Gates

explanation.surface: Streets in Gateshead, a town on the Tyne opposite Newcastle, run down to the boats.
explanation.walkthrough: Gateshead is a real town, but split as Gate's head it yields just the head of Gates.
explanation.definitionFit: A galley is the kitchen on a ship or boat, and boats are moored in a marina.

clue.text: Instrument you fake the sound of with hesitation

indicators.note: the sound of words means we want what they sound like when spoken, not their spelling

explanation.surface: Someone accused of only pretending to play, hesitantly.
explanation.definitionFit: A euphonium is a brass instrument like a small tuba, so it is an example of an instrument.

clue.text: Majestic Wendy and Lisa finally embraced by short returning aristocrat

indicators.note: finally points at the last letter of each of the names
something short is missing its end, so the last letter goes
returning means going back the way it came, so the word reads backwards
being embraced means being held inside another word's arms

blocks.note: last letters of Wendy and Lisa

explanation.surface: Prince's bandmates Wendy and Lisa are hugged by a nobleman.
explanation.walkthrough: Wendy Melvoin and Lisa Coleman played in The Revolution; LORD loses its D, turns round, and holds the two final letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Royal means befitting a king or queen, which is what majestic also describes.

clue.text: Old queen welcomes Troy Romeo who'll say "I would die for you"?

definitions.text: who'll say "I would die for you"?

indicators.note: welcoming someone means taking them in, so letters go inside

blocks.note: Mary I or Mary Queen of Scots
t is the abbreviation for troy weight

explanation.surface: A queen of old takes in a Romeo called Troy, who promises to die for her; 'I Would Die 4 U' is a Prince song.
explanation.walkthrough: Troy weight, used for precious metals, is abbreviated t; the old queen is one of the Marys of English or Scottish history.
explanation.definitionFit: A martyr is someone who dies for a cause or belief, so would say they would die for you.

clue.text: Rescue smart guy holding broken lav

indicators.note: something broken is out of its proper order, so its letters are rearranged
holding means having it inside, so one word wraps round the other

explanation.surface: A clever man tries to rescue a broken lavatory.
explanation.walkthrough: A lav is British slang for a toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: To salvage something is to save it from loss or wreckage, a verb synonym of rescue.

clue.text: A loopy circle around where price is displayed for sherry

indicators.note: around means going outside, so one word wraps the following phrase

blocks.note: a shop's price shows on the till
a circle is the shape of O

explanation.surface: A crazy loop around the spot where the price shows up.
explanation.walkthrough: MAD goes around ON TILL to make MONTILLAD, with A in front and O, the circle, at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Amontillado is a medium-dry Spanish sherry, so it is an example of the fortified wine.

clue.text: High percentage of ice cream

blocks.note: first meaning: as in 99 per cent, very nearly all
second meaning: a British soft-serve cone with a chocolate flake stuck in it

explanation.surface: Ice cream with a high fat content.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a 99 is a soft ice-cream cone with a Cadbury Flake chocolate bar pushed into it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ninety-nine per cent is near the top of the scale, and the 99 is a well-known British ice-cream cone.

clue.text: Western Arab's lute dubiously claimed with 12 as a basis

indicators.note: in an across answer going west means travelling right to left, so the word reads backwards
dubiously suggests something not done properly, so the letters come out in a wrong order

blocks.note: the oud is the lute of the Arab world

explanation.surface: A dubious claim about a western Arab's lute and the number twelve.
explanation.definitionFit: A duodecimal system counts in twelves rather than tens, so its numbers have twelve as their base.

clue.text: When doves cry, you'll hear these cold ducks primarily sympathising

definitions.text: When doves cry, you'll hear these

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter is used

blocks.note: a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, shaped like O

explanation.surface: A tender scene of cold ducks consoled; 'When Doves Cry' is Prince's hit single.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a duck is a batter's score of zero, and zero looks like O.
explanation.definitionFit: Doves make soft cooing calls, so the sounds you hear when they cry are their coos.

clue.text: Flier shows soldier lark's foot climbing support

indicators.note: in a down answer climbing means going upwards, so the word reads from bottom to top

blocks.note: the final letter, the foot, of lark
a tee supports a golf ball

explanation.surface: A soldier spots a skylark's foot on a climbing frame.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue the foot of a word is its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A parakeet is a small parrot, and as a bird it is something that flies.

clue.text: Squad rejoiced

blocks.note: first meaning: a team of people working together
second meaning: a past tense of crow, to exult

explanation.surface: The team celebrated.
explanation.walkthrough: Crew as the past tense of crow is an older form beside crowed.
explanation.definitionFit: A crew is a working team, and to crow is to exult, with crew as its old past tense.

clue.text: Clue for "could become grey"

blocks.note: the quoted word is the result the answer produces
the frame says the answer is itself a clue; its second word, up, is the instruction to mix the first

explanation.surface: A setter's note on how to clue a phrase about turning grey.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: read the answer as an instruction, CLOUD mixed up, and it produces 'could'.
explanation.definitionFit: When the sky clouds up it turns overcast and dull, so to cloud up is to become grey.

clue.text: The fleet oddly abandoned cadets sent out on a channel

indicators.note: oddly means the letters in odd-numbered positions are kept
abandoned means wild and unrestrained, so the letters run riot

blocks.note: first, third, fifth and seventh letters

explanation.surface: The navy left its trainees and dispatched them to sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Abandoned' reads as a verb, leaving the cadets behind, but it is an adjective meaning wild. Only CADETS actually change order.
explanation.definitionFit: To telecast is to broadcast by television, so a programme telecasted was sent out on a TV channel.

clue.text: Most soft and lustrous clothes of Dianne (Footloose actress)

indicators.note: clothes cover the outside, so only the outer letters of the name are kept

blocks.note: Dianne Wiest played the mother in Footloose (1984)

explanation.surface: Describing the soft, shiny costumes of an actress from the 1984 film Footloose.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracket looks like a gloss on Dianne, but it is a separate piece: her surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Dewy skin or eyes look moist, fresh and glowing, so the superlative means softest and most lustrous.

clue.text: Bobby, Apollonia and Mark Brown initially hula-hoop over grass

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so each name gives only its opening letter

blocks.note: first letters of the four names
a hoop has the shape of O
o is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: Prince's associates Bobby Z, Apollonia and BrownMark playing with a hula hoop.
explanation.definitionFit: Bamboo is a giant woody plant of the grass family, so it is an example of a grass.

clue.text: Your ass wanders into storage for relics

indicators.note: wandering means straying from a fixed path, so the letters move out of order

explanation.surface: Your donkey strays into a storeroom of holy relics.
explanation.definitionFit: An ossuary is a container or room for the bones of the dead, and saints' bones are kept as relics.

clue.text: Revere Computer Blue

blocks.note: the murderous computer in 2001: A Space Odyssey

explanation.surface: Treat the Prince song 'Computer Blue' with reverence.
explanation.definitionFit: To hallow something is to honour it as holy, so it is a synonym of revere.

clue.text: Darling Nikki protects retreating monarch

indicators.note: protecting means keeping something sheltered inside, so the answer lies within the phrase
retreating means moving backwards, so the letters are read in reverse

explanation.surface: Darling Nikki, from the Prince song of that name, shields a king in flight.
explanation.definitionFit: A king is a male sovereign, so the answer is a kind of monarch.

clue.text: Need remixed intro to Baby I'm A Star

indicators.note: a remix reworks a track, so these letters are reordered
the intro is the opening, so only the first letter is taken

explanation.surface: A request for a remix of the opening of Prince's song 'Baby I'm A Star'.
explanation.walkthrough: The song title is split: 'I'm A' merely links, and Star is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Deneb is the brightest star in the constellation Cygnus, so it is an example of a star.

clue.text: Krautrock band ultimately can leave Spandau

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so each word gives its final letter

blocks.note: last letters of the three words

explanation.surface: A German rock band can finally walk out of Spandau, the Berlin prison.
explanation.walkthrough: Krautrock is 1970s German experimental rock; Neu! was a Düsseldorf band in that style. Spandau Ballet was also a band.
explanation.definitionFit: Neu! were a leading German group of the krautrock movement, so they are an example of such a band.

clue.text: Travel for work that is about money and speed

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one abbreviation goes round the next word

explanation.surface: Someone justifying a business trip by the pay and the pace.
explanation.walkthrough: Tin is old British slang for money.
explanation.definitionFit: To itinerate is to travel from place to place, especially as a preacher or judge doing their job on circuit.

clue.text: Poland-America by United? Take me with you!

explanation.surface: A traveller pleads to come along on a United Airlines flight from Poland to America.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the plea a would-be guest makes to someone holding an invitation.
explanation.definitionFit: A plus-one is the extra guest an invitee may bring, so 'take me with you' is that person's request.

clue.text: Let's go crazy at start of tour, and wander off

indicators.note: crazy means wild and disordered, so the letters are scrambled
the start of a word is its first letter alone

explanation.surface: Fans going wild at the opening of Prince's tour, kicked off with 'Let's Go Crazy', then drifting away.
explanation.definitionFit: To get lost is to stray from the route, so it means to wander off and lose your way.
